passages.title: Grandfather's compound (unseen poem)
passages.text:
The compound is quiet now;
the cock that used to argue with the dawn
has gone the way of all proud things,
and the mango tree, older than my father's father,
drops its fruit for no one.

Grandfather sits where the shade is thickest,
counting the years on the beads of his cap,
each bead a season, each season a face
that has left for Lagos, for London, for the grave.

'You will come back,' he tells me,
and it is not a question.
The mango tree drops another fruit.
Somewhere a phone is ringing in a city
that does not know his name.

passages.title: Extract from a play (unseen)
passages.text:
MAMA RISI: (sweeping furiously) Twenty years I have sold pepper in this market. Twenty years! And now a boy with a clipboard tells me my stall is 'unauthorised'.
SEGUN: (not looking up from his phone) Mama, it is the new council policy. Everybody has to register.
MAMA RISI: Register! Did I register to be born? Did your father register before he died and left me with four children and this broom?
SEGUN: (quietly) Mama...
MAMA RISI: (stopping, staring at the broom) When they demolish this stall, Segun, what will I be? Tell me. A woman with a broom and no floor to sweep.
SEGUN: (putting the phone away at last) They will not demolish it. I filled the form for you last week. (He produces a folded paper.) Stall number forty-one. Your name. Twenty years, it says here, under 'experience'.
(MAMA RISI takes the paper. She does not read it. She holds it against her chest and resumes sweeping, slowly now.)

questions.B: she will not qualify for a trade discount

questions.subject: Commerce

questions.subject: Commerce

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Collective responsibility, whereby all ministers publicly support cabinet decisions or resign, is a feature of the
questions.explanation: Cabinet collective responsibility binds ministers in the parliamentary (Westminster) system.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In a confederation, the central authority is
questions.A: supreme over the units, which cannot secede
questions.B: elected directly by all citizens of the member states
questions.C: weak and dependent on the member states, which may secede
questions.D: responsible for all taxation in the member states
questions.explanation: A confederation is a loose union in which sovereignty stays with the member states.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of federalism for a country like Nigeria?
questions.A: it eliminates ethnic differences among the people
questions.B: it removes the need for a written constitution
questions.C: it makes government cheaper by reducing the number of officials
questions.D: it allows diverse groups to govern local affairs while remaining united
questions.explanation: Federalism accommodates diversity by giving component units autonomy within one nation.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: An ideology that emphasises private property, free markets and minimal government interference in the economy is
questions.explanation: Capitalism rests on private ownership and market allocation.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Britain is said to have an unwritten constitution because
questions.A: it has no rules regulating the conduct of government
questions.B: its laws are passed on by word of mouth alone
questions.C: its constitution is not contained in a single document
questions.D: parliament has no powers to make constitutional law
questions.explanation: British constitutional rules are scattered across statutes, conventions and judicial decisions rather than codified in one document.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A written constitution is an advantage for a federal state mainly because it
questions.A: can be changed easily whenever the need arises
questions.B: removes the need for political parties and elections
questions.C: abolishes the need for courts to settle disputes
questions.D: clearly defines the powers of each level of government
questions.explanation: A clear written division of powers prevents disputes between the centre and the units.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The 1999 Constitution provides that every arrested person must be charged to court within a reasonable time. This protects the citizen's right to
questions.explanation: Prompt arraignment guards against arbitrary detention — personal liberty.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the rule of law?
questions.explanation: Arbitrary arrest violates the rule of law.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A bill sponsored by an individual legislator rather than by the executive is called
questions.explanation: Bills introduced by individual members are private member's bills.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution, the annual estimates of revenue and expenditure (the Appropriation Bill) are prepared and laid before the National Assembly by
questions.explanation: Section 81 requires the President to prepare the estimates and lay them before each House of the National Assembly.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A child born in Lagos to two Ghanaian parents who are not Nigerian citizens is
questions.A: not a Nigerian citizen by birth under the 1999 Constitution
questions.B: automatically a Nigerian citizen by birth
questions.explanation: Nigerian citizenship by birth requires that a parent or grandparent belongs to an indigenous Nigerian community; birth on Nigerian soil alone is not enough.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following rights of a citizen may be lawfully restricted during a state of emergency?
questions.explanation: Freedom of movement may be curtailed (e.g. curfews) in an emergency; the right to life and freedom from torture cannot be derogated from.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The process of dividing a country into constituencies for electoral purposes is called
questions.explanation: Delimitation is the legitimate demarcation of constituencies; gerrymandering is manipulating boundaries for advantage.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A vote by the whole electorate on a specific question, such as approving a new constitution, is
questions.explanation: A referendum/plebiscite puts a question directly to the people.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: An election held to fill a seat that has become vacant through death or resignation before the end of the term is
questions.explanation: By-elections fill individual vacancies between general elections.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The right to vote in an election is called
questions.explanation: Franchise (suffrage) is the right to vote; universal adult suffrage extends it to all adults.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A party publishes a document setting out the policies it will pursue if elected. This document is
questions.explanation: A manifesto is a party's public declaration of its programme.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A major weakness of the one-party system is that it
questions.A: encourages too much opposition to government
questions.B: is too expensive for developing countries to run
questions.C: wastes public money on too many elections
questions.D: denies citizens a choice and can lead to dictatorship
questions.explanation: Without a legal opposition, the ruling party faces no electoral check.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) goes on strike to press the government to fund universities. Which method of pressure group activity is this?
questions.explanation: Strikes are industrial action, used by trade unions to force concessions.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A group formed to fight against the construction of a refuse dump near a village and dissolved after winning its case is
questions.explanation: Ad hoc groups form for a single issue and disband afterwards.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following is the most important channel for measuring public opinion in a modern democracy?
questions.B: the civil service and its records
questions.D: opinion polls and the mass media
questions.explanation: Polls and media (including social media) gauge and express public views on issues.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A civil servant who campaigns openly for a political party during an election violates the principle of
questions.explanation: Civil servants must serve any government of the day and stay out of partisan politics.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The head of the civil service in a ministry, responsible for its day-to-day administration and accounting, is the
questions.explanation: The permanent secretary is the administrative head and accounting officer of a ministry.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In the pre-colonial Hausa/Fulani emirate system, the Emir was assisted in administration by officials such as the
questions.explanation: The Waziri (chief adviser), Galadima and Madawaki were principal emirate officials.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A common feature of the Yoruba and Hausa/Fulani pre-colonial systems that made indirect rule easy to apply was
questions.A: a centralised system with recognised rulers
questions.B: the total absence of chiefs and kings
questions.C: republican assemblies of all adult males
questions.explanation: Both had kings/emirs with organised administrations through which the British could rule.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The amalgamation of the Northern and Southern Protectorates of Nigeria in 1914 was carried out by
questions.explanation: Lord Frederick Lugard amalgamated the two protectorates on 1 January 1914 and became the first Governor-General.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The French colonial policy that aimed to turn Africans into Frenchmen in culture and citizenship was
questions.explanation: Assimilation sought to absorb colonial subjects into French culture and political life.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Nigerian Youth Movement (NYM) of the 1930s is remembered as
questions.A: the first political party in Nigeria
questions.D: the first truly national political movement in Nigeria
questions.explanation: The NYM drew members from across regions, unlike the Lagos-based NNDP of Herbert Macaulay.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Herbert Macaulay is regarded as the father of Nigerian nationalism mainly because he
questions.A: founded the first Nigerian political party, the NNDP, in 1923
questions.B: led the army that resisted the British occupation
questions.C: wrote the 1922 Constitution for Sir Hugh Clifford
questions.explanation: The Nigerian National Democratic Party contested the Lagos seats created by the Clifford Constitution.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 was significant because it
questions.A: granted Nigeria full independence from Britain
questions.B: created the Senate as a second legislative chamber
questions.C: was drawn up after wide consultation with Nigerians
questions.D: abolished the three regions created by Richards
questions.explanation: Unlike the Richards Constitution, Macpherson's was preceded by consultations at village, provincial and regional levels.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Independence Constitution of 1960 provided for
questions.A: an executive president elected by the whole country
questions.B: a unitary government with power concentrated in Lagos
questions.C: a period of military rule before civilian government
questions.D: a parliamentary system with a Governor-General representing the Queen
questions.explanation: Nigeria became independent as a constitutional monarchy; it became a republic in 1963.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Under the 1963 Republican Constitution, the Queen of England was replaced as head of state by
questions.explanation: Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe became the ceremonial President while Tafawa Balewa remained Prime Minister.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: The Prime Minister of Nigeria during the First Republic was
questions.explanation: Balewa (NPC) was Prime Minister from 1957/1960 until the January 1966 coup.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: A major factor in the collapse of the First Republic was
questions.A: the census and election crises and regional rivalry
questions.B: the discovery of oil in commercial quantities
questions.C: the invasion of the country by foreign forces
questions.D: the creation of twelve states out of the regions
questions.explanation: The 1962/63 census dispute, the 1964 federal election and 1965 Western Region election crises destroyed confidence in the system.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The military government that created the first twelve states in Nigeria in 1967 was headed by
questions.explanation: Gowon replaced the four regions with twelve states on 27 May 1967.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Unification Decree No. 34 of 1966, which abolished federalism, was promulgated by
questions.explanation: Ironsi's decree turning Nigeria into a unitary state provoked the July 1966 counter-coup.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The President of Nigeria during the Second Republic was
questions.explanation: Shagari of the NPN was President from 1979 until the coup of 31 December 1983.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Buhari/Idiagbon regime of 1984–85 is best remembered for
questions.explanation: WAI promoted queue culture, punctuality and anti-corruption.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution, a President can serve a maximum of
questions.A: two terms of four years each
questions.explanation: Section 137 bars anyone who has been elected twice from contesting again.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The principle that appointments and resources should reflect the diversity of Nigeria's states and groups is called
questions.explanation: The federal character principle (s.14(3)) seeks to prevent domination by any group.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The body responsible for sharing federally collected revenue among the three tiers of government is the
questions.A: Central Bank of Nigeria's monetary policy committee
questions.D: Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission
questions.explanation: RMAFC advises on and monitors revenue allocation formulae.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The 1976 local government reform is important because it
questions.A: recognised local government as the third tier of government with uniform structure
questions.B: abolished local governments throughout the federation
questions.C: created seven additional states out of the existing twelve
questions.D: introduced indirect rule through traditional rulers
questions.explanation: The reform standardised local government nationwide and gave it constitutional recognition later in 1979.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A major problem of local governments in Nigeria is
questions.A: too much revenue from the federation account
questions.B: too many highly qualified staff on the payroll
questions.C: excessive control and interference by state governments
questions.D: lack of recognition in the 1999 Constitution
questions.explanation: State governments often withhold or divert local government funds and dissolve elected councils.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Public corporations were established mainly to
questions.A: make maximum profit for their private shareholders
questions.B: compete with the civil service for skilled staff
questions.C: provide employment for politicians who lost elections
questions.D: provide essential services that private firms might not supply adequately
questions.explanation: They provide utilities and services (power, water, rail) in the public interest.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following is a determinant of a country's foreign policy?
questions.A: its economic strength and national interest
questions.B: the weather and climate of the country
questions.C: the number of universities in the country
questions.D: the size and location of its capital city
questions.explanation: National interest, economy, military strength, geography and history shape foreign policy.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Commonwealth Prime Ministers' Conference held in Lagos in January 1966 was convened mainly to discuss
questions.A: Britain's role in the Suez crisis of 1956
questions.B: the threat of civil war in Nigeria
questions.D: the falling world price of cocoa and groundnuts
questions.explanation: Balewa hosted the first Commonwealth summit outside London to address Ian Smith's white-minority regime in Rhodesia.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The African Union replaced the Organisation of African Unity in
questions.explanation: The AU was launched in Durban in 2002; the OAU had been founded in 1963.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Commonwealth of Nations is an association of
questions.C: the major oil-producing states of the world
questions.D: mainly former British colonies and Britain
questions.explanation: Most members were once under British rule; Nigeria joined at independence in 1960.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria is a member of OPEC. The main aim of OPEC is to
questions.A: co-ordinate members' oil policies and stabilise oil prices
questions.C: promote free trade among African countries
questions.D: provide soft loans to poor oil-importing nations
questions.explanation: OPEC members coordinate production to influence prices in the world oil market.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'The classroom was a zoo after the teacher left' is an example of
questions.explanation: The classroom is directly called a zoo — a metaphor for noise and disorder.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers' illustrates
questions.explanation: Repetition of the initial /p/ consonant sound.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'The pen is mightier than the sword' uses
questions.explanation: 'Pen' stands for writing/ideas and 'sword' for force — things associated with them.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'Parting is such sweet sorrow' contains
questions.explanation: 'Sweet sorrow' places two contradictory terms side by side.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: A poet describes a storm raging while the hero grieves, as if nature shares his sorrow. This device is
questions.explanation: Attributing human emotions to nature to mirror a character's feelings is pathetic fallacy.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'Ten thousand saw I at a glance, tossing their heads in sprightly dance' — the second line uses
questions.explanation: The daffodils are given the human action of dancing and tossing heads.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: The repetition of a word at the beginning of successive clauses, as in 'We shall fight on the beaches, we shall fight on the landing grounds', is
questions.explanation: Anaphora is initial repetition for emphasis and rhythm.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'He was a lion in battle but a lamb at home' relies chiefly on
questions.explanation: Contrasting ideas (lion/lamb) in balanced form, each a metaphor.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A short, witty saying such as 'The only way to get rid of a temptation is to yield to it' is
questions.explanation: An epigram is a brief, pointed and often paradoxical statement.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A poem of praise addressed to a person, object or abstract idea, often in elevated language, is
questions.explanation: Odes celebrate their subject, e.g. 'Ode to a Nightingale'.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A narrative poem, often in four-line stanzas, telling a story of love or adventure and originally sung, is
questions.explanation: Ballads are simple narrative songs in quatrains with a refrain.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play that begins in misfortune but ends happily, mixing serious and comic elements, is
questions.explanation: Tragicomedy blends tragic and comic features with a happy resolution.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A humorous poem of five lines with an aabba rhyme scheme is
questions.explanation: Limericks are five-line comic verses rhyming aabba.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A speech delivered at the beginning of a play to introduce it is
questions.explanation: Prologue = before; epilogue = after.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The Japanese poetic form of three lines with seventeen syllables (5-7-5) is
questions.explanation: The haiku captures a moment, often from nature, in 17 syllables.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel opens with the hero already in prison and then recounts the events that led there. This technique is called
questions.explanation: Starting 'in the middle of things' and filling in the background later.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The time and place in which the action of a literary work occurs is its
questions.explanation: Setting includes physical place, historical period and social environment.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A secondary story that runs alongside the main plot of a novel is called
questions.explanation: Subplots parallel or contrast with the main action.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The purging of emotions of pity and fear that the audience experiences at the end of a tragedy is called
questions.explanation: Aristotle's catharsis is the emotional release produced by tragedy.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The excessive pride that leads a tragic hero to his downfall is called
questions.explanation: Hubris is overweening pride; nemesis is the retribution that follows.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A novel written entirely as the diary entries of the heroine uses
questions.B: the third-person omniscient point of view
questions.explanation: Diary form is a first-person narration.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A narrative technique that presents a character's thoughts as they flow, often without logical order or punctuation, is
questions.explanation: Stream of consciousness attempts to reproduce the flow of a mind.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The central idea or message that a literary work explores, such as 'the corrupting influence of power', is its
questions.explanation: A theme is the underlying idea, distinct from the events (plot).

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A character who represents a type — the wicked stepmother, the miserly old man — rather than an individual is
questions.explanation: Stock characters are conventional types recognisable across many works.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The character who opposes the hero and creates the main conflict is the
questions.explanation: The antagonist stands against the protagonist.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'The Lion and the Jewel', Lakunle's insistence on Western ways while refusing to pay the bride price presents him as
questions.A: a tragic hero destroyed by his ideals
questions.B: the true voice of village tradition
questions.C: a satirical portrait of half-baked modernity
questions.D: a chorus figure commenting on events
questions.explanation: Soyinka mocks Lakunle's shallow modernism, which cannot compete with Baroka's cunning.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'Second Class Citizen' by Buchi Emecheta, Adah's struggle in London mainly dramatises
questions.A: racial and gender discrimination against an African woman
questions.B: the joys and rewards of migrating to Britain
questions.C: the superiority of Western education over African
questions.D: the peaceful rhythm of life in an Igbo village
questions.explanation: Adah faces prejudice as a black immigrant and as a wife in an oppressive marriage.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'Unexpected Joy at Dawn' by Alex Agyei-Agyiri is set against the background of
questions.A: the Nigerian civil war and the blockade of Biafra
questions.B: the Ethiopian famine and the refugee crisis of the 1980s
questions.C: apartheid in South Africa and the Soweto uprising
questions.D: the 1983 expulsion of Ghanaians from Nigeria and Ghana's earlier expulsion of aliens
questions.explanation: The novel follows Nii and Mama Orojo across the Ghana–Nigeria border amid the expulsions.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'Wuthering Heights', Heathcliff's cruelty in adulthood is presented as rooted mainly in
questions.A: the humiliation and rejection he suffered as a boy and the loss of Catherine
questions.B: the sudden wealth he acquires during his absence
questions.C: the harsh education he received at Thrushcross Grange
questions.D: the strict religion preached to him by Joseph
questions.explanation: Hindley's degradation of him and Catherine's marriage to Edgar fuel his revenge.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'Look Back in Anger', Jimmy Porter's constant tirades chiefly express
questions.A: his deep contentment with life in post-war Britain
questions.B: his religious devotion and longing for the church
questions.C: the frustration and anger of the educated but powerless young
questions.D: his admiration for the upper class and its values
questions.explanation: Osborne's 'angry young man' rails against class, complacency and his own impotence.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In Niyi Osundare's 'The Leader and the Led', the animals' search for a leader ends with the choice of
questions.A: the lion, because of its strength and majesty
questions.B: no leader at all, since every animal is rejected
questions.C: the hyena, because it is cunning and fearless
questions.D: a leader who combines the lion's strength with the lamb's gentleness
questions.explanation: The poem argues that a good leader must be 'a lion and a lamb' — strong but humane.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Senghor's 'Black Woman' is best described as
questions.A: a celebration of African womanhood and, by extension, Africa itself
questions.B: a lament for the poet's dead mother
questions.C: a bitter protest against French colonial rule
questions.D: a love poem addressed to a European woman
questions.explanation: The poem praises the naked black woman as a symbol of the beauty of Africa.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In Maya Angelou's 'Caged Bird', the caged bird 'sings of freedom' because
questions.A: it is perfectly happy and contented in the cage
questions.B: the free bird taught it the song of freedom
questions.C: song is its only expression of longing for the freedom it is denied
questions.D: it wants its keeper to bring it food and water
questions.explanation: The caged bird's song is a cry of hope and protest against oppression.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: T. S. Eliot's 'The Journey of the Magi' presents the wise men's journey as
questions.A: easy, joyful and full of celebration
questions.B: a dream from which the speaker awakes
questions.C: a military expedition against a rival king
questions.explanation: 'A cold coming we had of it' — the birth brings a disturbing 'death' of their old world.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A poem whose lines do not rhyme and follow no regular metre is written in
questions.explanation: Free verse has neither rhyme nor fixed metre; blank verse has metre without rhyme.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables in a line of poetry is its
questions.explanation: Metre is the rhythmic structure; iambic pentameter is one example.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Two consecutive lines of poetry that rhyme and complete a thought form
questions.explanation: A rhyming pair of lines is a couplet.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The writer's attitude towards the subject or audience, as revealed by word choice, is called
questions.explanation: Tone is the author's attitude; mood is the feeling created in the reader.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the creation account of Genesis 1, God rested on the seventh day. This is given as the basis for
questions.explanation: Genesis 2:2–3 and Exodus 20:11 link the Sabbath rest to God's rest after creation.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At Mount Sinai the covenant between God and Israel was sealed when Moses
questions.A: built a golden calf at the foot of the mountain
questions.B: lifted up the bronze serpent in the wilderness
questions.C: struck the rock at Horeb and water came out
questions.D: sprinkled the blood of the sacrifice on the altar and on the people
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:8 — 'Behold the blood of the covenant which the Lord has made with you.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: God's covenant with Noah, signified by the rainbow, was a promise that
questions.A: God would never again destroy the earth with a flood
questions.B: the descendants of Noah would possess the land of Canaan
questions.C: Noah's descendants would be kings over all the earth
questions.D: the ark would be preserved for ever on Mount Ararat
questions.explanation: Genesis 9:11–17 — the rainbow is the sign that God will never again send a flood to destroy all flesh.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When the Israelites complained of thirst at Meribah, Moses struck the rock twice instead of speaking to it as commanded. As a result
questions.A: no water came out of the rock for the people
questions.B: Aaron was made leader of Israel in his place
questions.C: Moses was not allowed to enter the Promised Land
questions.D: the people were destroyed by a plague from God
questions.explanation: Numbers 20:12 — Moses and Aaron failed to honour God as holy before the people.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Joshua's leadership at Jericho shows that he
questions.B: bargained with the king of Jericho
questions.D: obeyed God's unusual instructions in faith
questions.explanation: Joshua 6 — the walls fell after seven days of marching and shouting as God directed.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The ravens that fed Elijah at the brook Cherith during the famine illustrate
questions.A: God's providence for those who obey Him
questions.B: the generosity of the people of Israel
questions.C: Elijah's skill in trapping birds for food
questions.D: the kindness of King Ahab towards the prophet
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17:4–6 — God commanded the ravens to bring bread and meat.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Abraham's readiness to sacrifice Isaac at Moriah demonstrates
questions.C: complete faith and obedience to God
questions.explanation: Genesis 22 — God provided a ram, and Abraham's faith was commended.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The failure of Samuel's sons Joel and Abijah as judges led the elders of Israel to
questions.A: appoint Saul as king without consulting Samuel
questions.B: stone Samuel for the sins of his sons
questions.C: propose a return to Egypt under a new leader
questions.D: demand a king like other nations
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 8:1–5 — the sons took bribes and perverted justice.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Achan's disobedience at Jericho consisted of
questions.A: taking some of the devoted things for himself
questions.B: worshipping Baal in the ruins of the city
questions.C: refusing to fight alongside the other tribes
questions.D: sparing the king of Jericho and his family
questions.explanation: Joshua 7 — his sin caused Israel's defeat at Ai; he and his family were stoned.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Lot's wife became a pillar of salt because she
questions.A: refused to leave Sodom with her husband
questions.B: stole silver and gold from the houses of Sodom
questions.C: looked back despite the angels' warning
questions.D: mocked the angels who came to rescue them
questions.explanation: Genesis 19:26 — disobedience and attachment to the doomed city.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: A Man after God's Own Heart
questions.q: David refused to kill Saul in the cave at En-gedi because
questions.A: he was afraid of Saul's army
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 24:6 — David would not stretch out his hand against the Lord's anointed.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: A Man after God's Own Heart
questions.q: David's friendship with Jonathan is remarkable because Jonathan
questions.A: stood to lose the throne to David yet loved and protected him
questions.B: had been David's bitter enemy at the court of Saul
questions.C: was a Philistine prince from the city of Gath
questions.D: later betrayed David's hiding place to Saul
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18–20 — Jonathan, Saul's heir, made a covenant with David.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When two women each claimed a living baby, Solomon ordered the child to be cut in two in order to
questions.A: punish both women for disturbing the court
questions.B: settle the case quickly and dismiss the women
questions.C: reveal the true mother through her compassion
questions.D: please the officials of the court with his wisdom
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:16–28 — the real mother begged that the child be spared.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Which statement best describes the effect of Ahab's greed for Naboth's vineyard?
questions.A: he gained the vineyard and prospered for many years
questions.B: Jezebel repented and restored the vineyard to Naboth's sons
questions.C: Naboth sold the vineyard willingly for a better one
questions.D: it led to murder, divine judgment and the fall of his house
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21 — Elijah pronounced that dogs would lick Ahab's blood and eat Jezebel.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the great image with a head of gold and feet of iron and clay, interpreted by Daniel, taught that
questions.A: earthly kingdoms rise and fall but God's kingdom endures
questions.B: Babylon would last for ever as the greatest kingdom
questions.C: gold is more valuable than iron and clay
questions.D: Daniel would become king over Babylon
questions.explanation: Daniel 2:44 — the stone cut without hands became a mountain filling the earth.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: King Hezekiah's reforms included
questions.A: building new high places for the worship of Baal
questions.B: making alliances with Assyria against Egypt
questions.C: removing the high places and breaking the bronze serpent Moses had made
questions.D: closing the temple and stopping the daily sacrifices
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 18:4 — the bronze serpent (Nehushtan) had become an object of worship.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Nehemiah's opponents Sanballat and Tobiah tried to stop the rebuilding of the wall by
questions.A: sending gifts to bribe the builders
questions.B: appealing to the priests to stop the work
questions.C: offering to help with the work in order to spy
questions.D: ridicule, threats of attack and false accusations
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 4–6 — the builders worked with weapons in hand and finished in 52 days.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Esther risked her life by going to the king uninvited in order to
questions.A: save the Jews from Haman's plot
questions.B: become queen in place of Vashti
questions.C: punish Mordecai for refusing to bow to Haman
questions.D: obtain wealth and honour for her family
questions.explanation: Esther 4:16 — 'If I perish, I perish.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The response of the people of Nineveh to Jonah's preaching was to
questions.A: stone him and throw his body into the sea
questions.B: ignore him and continue in their wickedness
questions.C: repent in sackcloth and ashes, from the king down
questions.D: expel him from the city and its surroundings
questions.explanation: Jonah 3:5–9 — the king decreed fasting for man and beast.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Social Justice, True Religion and Divine Love
questions.q: Micah 6:8 summarises what God requires of man as
questions.A: sacrifices and burnt offerings of year-old calves
questions.B: tithing all income and offering the first fruits
questions.C: fasting twice a week and praying in the temple
questions.D: to do justice, love kindness and walk humbly with God
questions.explanation: Micah rejects mere ritual in favour of justice, mercy and humility.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Social Justice, True Religion and Divine Love
questions.q: Amos condemned the women of Samaria as 'cows of Bashan' because they
questions.A: oppressed the poor and demanded luxury from their husbands
questions.B: were farmers who neglected the temple
questions.C: refused to marry and bear children
questions.D: worshipped golden cows at Bethel and Dan
questions.explanation: Amos 4:1 — they crushed the needy to feed their indulgence.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When God called Jeremiah, Jeremiah objected that he
questions.A: was too old to travel and preach
questions.B: was a sinner with unclean lips
questions.C: was only a youth and could not speak
questions.D: was a foreigner and not of the priestly line
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 1:6 — God touched his mouth and put His words there.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jeremiah promised a 'new covenant' under which God would
questions.A: give a new set of stone tablets
questions.D: write His law on the people's hearts
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:31–34 — under the new covenant the law would be written on hearts, not on stone, and all would know the Lord.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Birth and Early Life of Jesus
questions.q: When Jesus was presented in the temple, Simeon declared that the child would be
questions.A: a light for revelation to the Gentiles and glory to Israel
questions.B: a king like David who would defeat the Romans
questions.C: a priest like Aaron serving in the temple
questions.D: a prophet like Elijah who would call down fire
questions.explanation: Luke 2:29–32 (the Nunc Dimittis).

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Birth and Early Life of Jesus
questions.q: At twelve years old Jesus was found in the temple
questions.A: driving out the traders and money-changers
questions.B: healing the sick and casting out demons
questions.C: sitting among the teachers, listening and asking questions
questions.D: hiding from the soldiers of King Herod
questions.explanation: Luke 2:46 — 'Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.q: At Jesus' baptism, the voice from heaven said,
questions.B: 'Repent, for the kingdom is at hand'
questions.D: 'This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased'
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:17; the Spirit descended like a dove.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus called Matthew (Levi) while he was
questions.explanation: Matthew 9:9 — and Jesus then ate with tax collectors and sinners.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said that anyone who wishes to be His disciple must
questions.A: sell everything and give the money to the temple
questions.B: become a Pharisee and keep the whole law
questions.C: deny himself, take up his cross and follow Him
questions.D: fast every day and pray in the synagogue
questions.explanation: Mark 8:34 — self-denial and cross-bearing are the conditions of discipleship.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At the wedding in Cana, Jesus turned water into wine. John calls this
questions.A: a parable about the coming kingdom of God
questions.B: a fulfilment of the law given through Moses
questions.C: a temptation which Jesus overcame at the feast
questions.D: the first of His signs, which manifested His glory
questions.explanation: John 2:11 — the first sign at Cana revealed His glory and His disciples believed in Him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The raising of Lazarus at Bethany demonstrated that Jesus is
questions.explanation: John 11:25 — 'I am the resurrection and the life.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Jesus stilled the storm on the Sea of Galilee, the disciples asked,
questions.A: 'Who then is this, that even wind and sea obey him?'
questions.B: 'Are you the King of the Jews who was promised?'
questions.C: 'Lord, should we call down fire from heaven?'
questions.D: 'Where shall we buy bread for all these people?'
questions.explanation: Mark 4:41 — the miracle revealed His authority over nature.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the sower, the seed that fell among thorns represents those who
questions.B: receive it with joy but fall away in persecution
questions.C: hear the word but the cares of the world and the love of riches choke it
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:22 — the thorns stand for worldly cares and the deceitfulness of riches that choke the word.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the talents, the servant who buried his one talent was condemned because he
questions.A: lost the money in a bad trade
questions.B: gave it away to the poor without permission
questions.C: stole it and fled to another country
questions.D: made no effort to use what he was given
questions.explanation: Matthew 25:24–30 — 'You wicked and slothful servant.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The parable of the prodigal son teaches chiefly about
questions.A: God's readiness to forgive the repentant sinner
questions.B: the danger of wealth to a young man
questions.C: the duties of servants to their master
questions.D: the judgment at the end of the world
questions.explanation: Luke 15:11–32 — the father runs to meet the returning son.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: 'Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called',
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:9 — peacemakers reflect the character of God and are therefore called His children.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus taught that when giving alms, one should not let the left hand know what the right hand is doing, in order to
questions.A: keep one's accounts secret from tax collectors
questions.B: be able to give more than the Pharisees
questions.C: avoid giving for the praise of men
questions.D: prevent the poor from knowing who gave
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:1–4 — reward comes from the Father who sees in secret.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Jesus sent out the twelve, He told them to take
questions.A: two tunics and enough money for the journey
questions.B: letters of introduction to the synagogue rulers
questions.C: swords and staffs to defend themselves
questions.D: no gold, silver, bag or extra tunic, relying on hospitality
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:9–10 — 'the labourer deserves his food.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.q: Jesus entered Jerusalem riding on a donkey to fulfil the prophecy of
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:9 — 'your king comes to you, humble and mounted on a donkey.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At the Last Supper Jesus identified His betrayer as
questions.A: Peter, who would deny Him three times
questions.B: the one who dipped his hand in the dish with Him
questions.D: John, the disciple whom He loved
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:23; Judas then went out.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Trials and the Death of Jesus
questions.q: Peter denied Jesus three times, as Jesus had foretold, before
questions.explanation: Luke 22:61 — Peter went out and wept bitterly.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Trials and the Death of Jesus
questions.q: At the moment Jesus died, the curtain of the temple was torn in two, signifying
questions.A: the coming destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans
questions.B: that the way to God was now open to all through Christ
questions.C: nothing more than the effect of the earthquake
questions.D: the end of the Sabbath and the start of the Passover
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:51; Hebrews 10:19–20.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Before ascending, Jesus commissioned the disciples to
questions.A: build a new temple in Jerusalem
questions.C: return to their fishing in Galilee
questions.D: raise an army and fight against Rome
questions.explanation: Matthew 28:19–20 — the Great Commission.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'I am the way, the truth and the life' in answer to a question from
questions.explanation: John 14:5–6 — Thomas asked how they could know the way.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said the greatest commandment is to love God, and the second is to
questions.C: honour the priests and the elders
questions.D: pay tithes of all that you earn
questions.explanation: Matthew 22:37–39 — love of God and love of neighbour sum up the Law and the Prophets.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The early believers in Jerusalem 'had all things in common' and
questions.A: kept their property secret from the apostles
questions.B: sold their possessions and shared with anyone in need
questions.D: stopped praying in the temple with the Jews
questions.explanation: Acts 2:44–45 and 4:32–35 — believers sold property and distributed the proceeds so that none was in need.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Holy Spirit and the Mission of the Church
questions.q: Before Pentecost Jesus told the apostles to wait in Jerusalem for
questions.A: the destruction of the temple that He had foretold
questions.B: the promise of the Father — power from the Holy Spirit
questions.C: the arrival of Paul from Tarsus to lead them
questions.D: the Roman census ordered by the emperor
questions.explanation: Acts 1:4–8 — the Spirit would give them power to be witnesses in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria and to the ends of the earth.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Stephen, the first Christian martyr, prayed as he was stoned:
questions.B: 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them'
questions.explanation: Acts 7:60 — echoing Jesus on the cross; Saul approved of the killing.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Saul's conversion took place
questions.explanation: Acts 9 — a light from heaven and the voice, 'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The disciples were first called Christians in
questions.explanation: Acts 11:26 — at Antioch, where Barnabas and Saul taught for a whole year, the disciples were first called Christians.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul taught that 'all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God' and are justified
questions.A: by faithfully keeping the works of the law
questions.B: freely by God's grace through the redemption in Christ Jesus
questions.C: by circumcision according to the custom of Moses
questions.D: by offering sacrifices in the temple at Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Romans 3:23–24 — justification is a free gift of grace, not something earned by keeping the law.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul listed the fruit of the Spirit as love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
questions.explanation: Galatians 5:22–23 — the nine-fold fruit of the Spirit ends with gentleness and self-control.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus taught humility at a feast by advising guests to
questions.A: take the highest seat before anyone else
questions.B: take the lowest place so that the host may invite them higher
questions.C: leave early so as not to trouble the host
questions.D: bring gifts that are worthy of the host
questions.explanation: Luke 14:7–11 — 'whoever exalts himself will be humbled.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Peter asked how often he should forgive his brother, Jesus replied
questions.explanation: Matthew 18:22 — unlimited forgiveness.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul said that of the gifts of prophecy, tongues and knowledge, the one to be most desired for building up the church is
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:1–5 — prophecy edifies the whole church; tongues need interpretation.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus praised the poor widow who put two small coins in the treasury because she
questions.A: gave the most money of all the worshippers
questions.B: gave all she had to live on
questions.C: gave secretly so that no one would see her
questions.D: gave gold coins rather than copper ones
questions.explanation: Mark 12:41–44 — Jesus measured the gift by sacrifice, not by amount: she gave everything she had.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When asked whether it was lawful to pay tax to Caesar, Jesus answered,
questions.A: 'Do not pay, for Caesar has no authority over the children of God'
questions.B: 'Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's'
questions.C: 'Pay only the temple tax, and let Caesar collect his own'
questions.D: 'Caesar is a thief who robs the poor of what belongs to God'
questions.explanation: Mark 12:17 — the answer escaped the trap and set out the Christian duty to both state and God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul supported himself during his missionary work by
questions.explanation: Acts 18:3 — he worked with Aquila and Priscilla.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The parable of the ten virgins teaches that believers should
questions.A: sleep early so as to be strong for the feast
questions.B: be ready always, since the hour of His return is unknown
questions.C: buy enough oil to sell to their neighbours
questions.D: avoid weddings that take place at night
questions.explanation: Matthew 25:1–13 — 'Watch therefore.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Peter declared 'God shows no partiality' after
questions.A: the decision of the Council of Jerusalem on circumcision
questions.B: seeing the Holy Spirit fall on Cornelius and his household
questions.C: healing the lame man at the Beautiful Gate
questions.D: his miraculous release from Herod's prison
questions.explanation: Acts 10:34–35, 44 — the Spirit fell on Gentiles in the house of Cornelius, proving that God accepts every nation.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the persistent widow, Jesus taught that we should
questions.A: give up when prayers are not answered
questions.B: always pray and not lose heart
questions.explanation: Luke 18:1–8 — if an unjust judge finally answers a persistent widow, God will surely answer His people who cry to Him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector, the tax collector was justified because he
questions.A: gave tithes of all that he earned
questions.B: humbly asked for mercy as a sinner
questions.C: prayed longer than the Pharisee did
questions.D: stood at the front of the temple to pray
questions.explanation: Luke 18:9–14 — 'God, be merciful to me, a sinner.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul told the Romans, 'If your enemy is hungry, feed him' in order to
questions.explanation: Romans 12:20–21 — kindness to an enemy heaps burning coals on his head and overcomes evil with good.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Zacchaeus, after meeting Jesus, promised to
questions.A: leave Jericho and follow Jesus to Jerusalem
questions.B: give half his goods to the poor and repay fourfold what he had taken
questions.C: build a synagogue for the people of Jericho
questions.D: become one of the twelve disciples immediately
questions.explanation: Luke 19:8 — restitution as a fruit of repentance.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: David's adultery with Bathsheba led directly to
questions.A: the death of Saul on Mount Gilboa
questions.B: the murder of Uriah and the death of the child
questions.C: the division of the kingdom into Israel and Judah
questions.D: a long and bitter war with the Philistines
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 11–12 — David arranged Uriah's death to hide the adultery, and Nathan announced that the child would die.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) over a period of about
questions.explanation: From the first revelation (about 610 CE) to his death in 632 CE — roughly 23 years, 13 in Makkah and 10 in Madinah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Surahs revealed in Makkah generally deal with
questions.B: faith in Allah, the Hereafter and moral warning
questions.D: relations with the Jews of Madinah
questions.explanation: Makkan surahs are short and focus on Tawhid, the Day of Judgment and warning; Madinan surahs contain detailed law.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Surah Al-Kawthar reminds the Prophet that Allah has given him abundance and commands him to
questions.B: pray to his Lord and sacrifice
questions.explanation: Surah 108:2 — 'So pray to your Lord and sacrifice.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Surah An-Nasr announces the coming of Allah's help and victory and people entering Islam in crowds. It refers to
questions.explanation: Surah 110 was revealed near the end of the Prophet's life, foreshadowing the conquest and his passing.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The verse 'Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it' is from Surah
questions.explanation: Surah 99:7–8 stresses accountability for every deed.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Hadith whose chain of transmission is unbroken and whose narrators are all reliable is classified as
questions.explanation: Sahih Hadith meet the strictest conditions; Bukhari and Muslim are the most authoritative collections.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said, 'Religion is sincerity (nasihah)'. When asked to whom, he replied:
questions.A: to Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims and their common people
questions.B: to the wealthy, the rulers and the learned men of the community
questions.C: to one's parents, spouse, children and close relatives only
questions.D: to the scholars, the imams and the judges of the Muslims only
questions.explanation: Reported by Muslim; sincerity and good counsel are owed at every level.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said, 'Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim.' A Muslim girl who is denied schooling is being deprived of
questions.explanation: The Hadith (Ibn Majah) makes learning compulsory for male and female alike.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said that a Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand
questions.explanation: Reported by Bukhari; Islam requires that others be safe from one's speech and actions.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: The declaration 'La ilaha illa Allah, Muhammadur Rasulullah' is called the
questions.explanation: The Shahadah is the first pillar of Islam and the entry into the faith.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: A man believes in Allah but also consults a fortune-teller and acts on his predictions. According to a Hadith, his prayers
questions.A: are doubled in reward because of his faith
questions.B: will not be accepted for forty days
questions.C: are unaffected so long as he still prays
questions.explanation: Reported by Muslim; belief in soothsayers contradicts trust in Allah's knowledge of the unseen.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The attribute of Allah meaning 'the Provider' is
questions.explanation: Ar-Razzaq is the Sustainer who provides for all creatures; Al-Khaliq is the Creator.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) defined Ihsan as
questions.A: to fast in Ramadan and stand in prayer at night
questions.B: to worship Allah as though you see Him, knowing that He sees you
questions.C: to give Zakat and sadaqah generously to the poor
questions.D: to perform Hajj and Umrah as often as one is able
questions.explanation: The Hadith of Jibril distinguishes Islam, Iman and Ihsan.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Muslims believe that the Qur'an, the Tawrat, the Zabur and the Injil were revealed respectively to
questions.explanation: Belief in the revealed books is the third article of faith.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Belief in the Last Day (Yawm al-Qiyamah) influences a Muslim's conduct mainly by
questions.A: making him fear people more than he fears Allah
questions.B: reminding him that every deed will be judged and rewarded or punished
questions.C: encouraging him to acquire wealth before the end comes
questions.D: removing his personal responsibility for his actions
questions.explanation: Accountability in the Hereafter is the strongest motive for righteous conduct.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The five pillars of Islam are the Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and
questions.explanation: Hajj is the fifth pillar, obligatory once for those able.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The call to prayer (adhan) was first made in Madinah by
questions.explanation: Bilal, a freed Abyssinian slave, was the first mu'adhdhin.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following invalidates wudu (ablution)?
questions.explanation: Deep sleep, answering the call of nature and passing wind nullify wudu.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Friday congregational prayer (Jumu'ah) replaces
questions.explanation: Jumu'ah, with its two sermons, takes the place of Zuhr on Fridays for those obliged to attend.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim who deliberately misses Zuhr must
questions.A: pay a fine to the mosque as expiation
questions.B: make it up (qada) as soon as possible and seek forgiveness
questions.C: fast for one day in place of the prayer
questions.D: double the number of rak'ahs in the next Asr
questions.explanation: Missed obligatory prayers are made up; repentance is required for deliberate neglect.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A farmer harvests 1,000 kg of maize from land watered only by rain. The Zakat due is
questions.explanation: Produce from rain-fed land pays 'ushr (one-tenth); irrigated land pays half of that (5%).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Zakat differs from sadaqah in that Zakat is
questions.A: voluntary and left to the giver's conscience
questions.B: obligatory with fixed rates and recipients
questions.C: given only in the last ten days of Ramadan
questions.D: given only to poor relatives and neighbours
questions.explanation: Zakat is a compulsory pillar; sadaqah is voluntary charity of any amount at any time.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The night in Ramadan described in the Qur'an as 'better than a thousand months' is
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Qadr (97); it falls in the last ten nights of Ramadan.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A man deliberately eats during a Ramadan fast without any excuse. In addition to repentance, the expiation (kaffarah) prescribed for deliberately breaking the fast is
questions.A: feeding one poor person for each day missed
questions.B: fasting two consecutive months, or feeding sixty poor people
questions.C: paying Zakat twice in that year
questions.D: performing Umrah before the next Ramadan
questions.explanation: The Hadith on the man who broke his fast prescribes freeing a slave, then two months' fasting, then feeding sixty.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The pre-dawn meal taken before fasting is called
questions.explanation: Suhur is recommended by the Prophet as a blessed meal; iftar is the meal that breaks the fast.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The state of consecration that a pilgrim enters, marked for men by two white unsewn cloths, is called
questions.explanation: Ihram involves specific clothing, intention and prohibitions (no perfume, hunting, cutting hair).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The stoning of the pillars at Mina commemorates
questions.A: the Prophet's victory over the Quraysh at Badr
questions.B: Ibrahim's rejection of Satan's temptation at the sacrifice
questions.C: the destruction of Abrahah's army of elephants
questions.D: the digging of the well of Zamzam by Abdul-Muttalib
questions.explanation: Ibrahim threw stones at Shaytan who tried to dissuade him from obeying Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The lesser pilgrimage that can be performed at any time of the year is
questions.explanation: Umrah consists of ihram, tawaf, sa'y and shaving/cutting hair, without Arafah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A student who refuses to cheat in an examination although everyone around her is cheating is practising
questions.A: hijrah (migration for the sake of Allah)
questions.explanation: Resisting one's desires to obey Allah is the greater jihad.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Before prophethood, Muhammad (SAW) worked as a trader for a wealthy widow whom he later married. She was
questions.explanation: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid was the first to believe in his mission.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) was orphaned early: his father died before his birth and his mother Aminah died when he was about
questions.explanation: He was then cared for by his grandfather Abdul-Muttalib and later his uncle Abu Talib.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The 'Year of Sorrow' ('Am al-Huzn) refers to the year in which
questions.A: the Prophet lost his wife Khadijah and his uncle Abu Talib
questions.B: the Muslims lost the battle of Uhud and Hamzah was killed
questions.C: the Prophet was forced to leave Makkah for Madinah
questions.D: Ibrahim, the Prophet's infant son, died in Madinah
questions.explanation: Both deaths in about 619 CE removed his chief supporters and exposed him to greater persecution.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: When the people of Ta'if rejected the Prophet (SAW) and stoned him, he
questions.A: cursed them and asked Allah to destroy the town
questions.B: prayed that their descendants would accept Islam
questions.C: sent an army from Madinah to punish them
questions.D: abandoned his mission and returned to trading
questions.explanation: He refused the angel's offer to crush them between the mountains.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The first mosque built by the Prophet (SAW) after leaving Makkah was at
questions.explanation: Masjid Quba was built on the outskirts of Madinah before he entered the city.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: On the night of the Hijrah, the person who slept in the Prophet's bed to deceive the Quraysh assassins was
questions.explanation: Ali risked his life and later returned the trusts held by the Prophet to their owners.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Leader
questions.q: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (6 AH), which seemed unfavourable to the Muslims, is called a 'clear victory' in the Qur'an because it
questions.B: brought peace that allowed Islam to spread rapidly
questions.D: made the Quraysh Muslims at once
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Fath (48:1); more people entered Islam in the following two years than in all the years before.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Model
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) mended his own clothes, milked his goats and helped with housework. This teaches that
questions.A: a leader should not be seen doing menial work
questions.B: humility and service in the home are part of good character
questions.C: men should stay at home and not work outside
questions.D: housework should be left to servants and slaves
questions.explanation: Aisha reported that he 'was in the service of his family' at home.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The caliph who standardised the text of the Qur'an and sent copies to the provinces, burning variant copies, was
questions.explanation: Uthman's recension (about 650 CE) preserved a single authoritative text.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Abu Bakr's first major challenge as caliph was
questions.A: the conquest of the Persian empire
questions.B: the Riddah wars against tribes that refused to pay Zakat
questions.C: the compilation of the Hadith into books
questions.D: the building of the garrison city of Kufah
questions.explanation: He insisted that Zakat was inseparable from Salah and restored the unity of Arabia.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Caliph Ali moved the capital of the caliphate from Madinah to
questions.explanation: Kufah in Iraq became his base during the civil strife (fitnah).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Ansar were
questions.A: the Makkan Muslims who emigrated to Madinah
questions.B: the Muslims of Madinah who welcomed and helped the emigrants
questions.C: the Jewish tribes living in Madinah
questions.D: the Quraysh leaders who opposed the Prophet
questions.explanation: Ansar means 'helpers'; the emigrants were the Muhajirun.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: In Islam a husband is required to provide his wife with maintenance (nafaqah), which includes
questions.A: only food, since clothing is her own responsibility
questions.B: food, clothing and shelter according to his means
questions.C: a car and a house in her own name
questions.D: nothing at all if she has wealth of her own
questions.explanation: Qur'an 65:7 — 'Let the wealthy man spend according to his means.'

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A husband pronounces one revocable divorce (talaq). During the wife's iddah he
questions.A: cannot take her back under any circumstances
questions.B: may take her back without a new contract
questions.C: must pay a second mahr before taking her back
questions.D: must obtain a court order before taking her back
questions.explanation: Reconciliation (raj'ah) is permitted during the iddah of a revocable divorce.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The dissolution of marriage initiated by the wife, in which she returns the mahr or compensation, is
questions.explanation: Khul' is the wife's right to seek release from the marriage.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Rights and Duties of Parents and Children
questions.q: When asked who deserves the best companionship, the Prophet (SAW) said 'Your mother' three times before saying
questions.explanation: Reported by Bukhari and Muslim, stressing the mother's special status.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Rights and Duties of Parents and Children
questions.q: Parents' duties to children in Islam include
questions.A: giving them a good name, education and fair treatment
questions.B: leaving them to fend for themselves from an early age
questions.C: favouring sons over daughters in gifts and inheritance
questions.D: denying them any share of the family inheritance
questions.explanation: The Prophet stressed good names, teaching and equal gifts among children.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said that Jibril kept urging him about the rights of the neighbour until he thought the neighbour would
questions.explanation: Reported by Bukhari; a Muslim must not harm his neighbour and should share with him.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: In his Farewell Sermon the Prophet (SAW) declared that an Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab except by
questions.explanation: The sermon abolished racial and tribal superiority.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: When a noble woman of Makhzum was caught stealing and people sought to excuse her, the Prophet (SAW) said that earlier nations were destroyed because
questions.A: they were poor and had nothing to give in charity
questions.B: they punished the weak but spared the noble when they stole
questions.C: they prayed too little and fasted too rarely
questions.D: they traded on Fridays instead of attending prayer
questions.explanation: He added that if Fatimah his daughter stole he would cut off her hand — equality before the law.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Before prophethood the Makkans entrusted their valuables to Muhammad (SAW) and called him
questions.explanation: Al-Amin means 'the trustworthy'; As-Siddiq was Abu Bakr and Al-Faruq was Umar.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said, 'Beware of the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no barrier between it and Allah.' This warns
questions.explanation: Reported by Bukhari; oppression (zulm) will be darkness on the Day of Judgment.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Hoarding foodstuffs to force prices up (ihtikar) is
questions.B: forbidden because it harms the community
questions.explanation: The Prophet said only a sinner hoards.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following business arrangements is permitted in Islam?
questions.A: a loan repaid with a fixed rate of interest
questions.C: a pool for betting on football results
questions.D: a shop that sells wine to non-Muslims only
questions.explanation: Mudarabah shares real profit and loss; riba, maysir (gambling) and khamr are forbidden.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim is allowed to eat forbidden food only when
questions.A: he is travelling a long distance from home
questions.B: he is starving and no lawful food can be found
questions.C: it is cheaper than the lawful food available
questions.D: a non-Muslim host offers it out of hospitality
questions.explanation: Qur'an 2:173 — necessity permits the forbidden without wilful disobedience or excess.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Under Umar ibn al-Khattab, the treasury (Bayt al-Mal) paid stipends to
questions.A: soldiers only, in proportion to their rank
questions.B: all Muslims on a register (diwan), including widows and the poor
questions.C: the caliph's family and close companions only
questions.D: the Quraysh only, as the Prophet's tribe
questions.explanation: Umar's diwan organised state payments.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Umar chose his successor by
questions.A: naming his son Abdullah as the next caliph
questions.B: appointing a council of six companions to choose from among themselves
questions.C: holding a general election among all Muslims
questions.D: leaving the matter to the commanders of the army
questions.explanation: The shura of six (including Uthman and Ali) chose Uthman.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) received the Christian delegation from Najran in his mosque and allowed them to pray there. This shows
questions.B: tolerance and respect for people of other faiths
questions.D: that prayer direction does not matter
questions.explanation: The Najran Christians were treated as guests and given a treaty of protection.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Muslims lost the advantage at the battle of Uhud mainly because
questions.A: the archers left their post on the hill to collect booty
questions.B: they had no leader after the Prophet was wounded
questions.C: heavy rain prevented them from using their bows
questions.D: the Quraysh were three times more numerous
questions.explanation: Khalid ibn al-Walid's cavalry attacked from the rear once the hill was abandoned.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islam first reached West Africa, including Kanem-Bornu and later Hausaland, mainly through
questions.A: military conquest by Arab armies from Egypt
questions.C: European missionaries who arrived by sea
questions.D: the sea route from India and the Persian Gulf
questions.explanation: Berber and Arab traders and Wangara scholars spread Islam peacefully along trade routes.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Sokoto Jihad of 1804 was led by
questions.explanation: Shehu Uthman dan Fodio established the Sokoto Caliphate.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Islam's view of the environment is that man is
questions.A: free to exploit nature in any way he likes
questions.B: a khalifah (steward) answerable to Allah for creation
questions.C: not responsible for the welfare of animals
questions.D: forbidden to farm or cut down any tree
questions.explanation: Qur'an 2:30; the Prophet forbade wastefulness even when making wudu from a flowing river.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which Islamic principle most directly addresses examination malpractice?
questions.B: amanah (trust) and the prohibition of cheating
questions.explanation: Cheating breaks trust and the Prophet said the cheat is 'not one of us'.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim who prays in congregation earns a reward, according to the Hadith, of
questions.B: twenty-seven times that of praying alone
questions.explanation: Reported by Bukhari and Muslim.
